title: Itrax micro X-ray fluorescence (μXRF) for soft biological tissues
author: Gadd, Gopi, et al.

steps.title: Thaw and dissect samples
steps.instruction: Remove the frozen prawns from the freezer, allow them to thaw, then remove the exoskeleton together with the hindgut and gonads and rinse the specimens with deionized water to eliminate contaminants.

steps.title: Excise abdominal tissue
steps.instruction: Using a clean stainless‑steel scalpel, cut a 5 cm² section of abdominal tissue from the ventral side, rinse the tissue again with deionized water, and transfer it into a clean, dry petri dish with clean forceps.

steps.title: Dry tissue in oven
steps.instruction: Label the petri dish and place it in an oven set to approximately 60 °C for 48 h to ensure the sample is completely dry.

steps.title: Grind to fine powder
steps.instruction: Grind the dried tissue into a fine, homogeneous powder using a mortar and pestle; clean the mortar and pestle with 70 % ethanol between each sample.

steps.title: Store powdered sample
steps.instruction: Transfer the fine powder into a clean glass vial, cap it to prevent moisture ingress, store the vial in a desiccator, and for long‑term storage vacuum‑pack the vial and keep it in a freezer at –17 to –20 °C.

steps.title: Prepare Perspex sample holder
steps.instruction: Clean a Perspex sample holder (originally for wood) with ethanol, apply a layer of clear double‑sided sticky tape across its middle, mark 2 cm intervals on the tape, place about 1 cm of masking tape between the intervals, leave a 0.5 mm gap from the double‑sided tape, and cover the top and bottom of the holder with masking tape leaving roughly 2 cm gaps, creating a grid of squares each about 4 cm².

steps.title: Load powder onto holder
steps.instruction: Transfer approximately 2 g of the powdered sample into each square of the grid and label the corresponding masking tape.

steps.title: Flatten powder layer
steps.instruction: Flatten each powder deposit to an approximate thickness of 2 mm.

steps.title: Scan sample with Itrax
steps.instruction: Place the prepared sample holder into the Itrax μXRF instrument for scanning.

steps.title: Standardize count data
steps.instruction: Collect element counts at 1 mm intervals, standardize the data to obtain relative abundance for every element, acquire 20 data points per sample and average them to minimise heterogeneity effects.

steps.title: Validate with neutron activation analysis
steps.instruction: Scan around 60 individual P. monodon samples on the Itrax and validate the semi‑quantitative trends using neutron activation analysis (NAA).

steps.title: Perform statistical analysis
steps.instruction: Use the standardized elemental data for the required statistical analyses, such as determining the provenance of tiger prawns.
